subject.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server reply-session-init conflict leaves the session with no transcript mirror → tool-results silently return empty with no self-heal

question: Which component should own recovery when a reply-session initialization conflict leaves a Codex app-server session without usable mirrored history or thread binding?
rationale: The source issue spans shared reply-session initialization, Codex app-server binding generation, mirrored-history replay, and channel retries, and current main has changed the binding model since the report's sidecar diagnosis.

options.title: Codex/session-owned recovery
options.body: Add targeted recovery in the Codex/session runtime after verifying binding generation and replay safety, leaving channel retries as a backup for inbound delivery only.

options.title: Shared reply-session retry or queue
options.body: Broaden the core reply-session initialization conflict handling so stale snapshots wait, retry, or take over before any runtime-specific recovery is needed.

options.title: Channel retry only
options.body: Rely on Telegram/Slack-style ingress retries, accepting that missing Codex mirrored-history and tool-result routing invariants remain owned elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Codex/session-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Add targeted recovery in the Codex/session runtime after verifying binding generation and replay safety, leaving channel retries as a backup for inbound delivery only.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent SQLite binding migration makes the Codex binding/session boundary the most central decision point before repair.
